fact: São Tomé and Príncipe regulators, including the head of its Institute of Innovation and Knowledge, took part in a UNESCO data governance workshop in Maputo, 8 to 10 December 2025, organised with Mozambique's INTIC and Smart Africa, aligned with the Smart Africa Data Governance Blueprint and the African Union Data Policy Framework.

Sao Tome and Principe was among six countries whose policymakers and experts attended the Second Lusophone Africa Data Governance Workshop in Luanda on 15-17 June 2026, co-hosted by Angola's data protection agency, Smart Africa, the World Bank, CETIC.br and UNESCO; attendance only, no agreement signed (the document is dated 28 July 2026, the event June).

AUDA-NEPAD launched its Programme for African Developing Island Economies on 24 July 2026 at an African Union ministerial segment in Abidjan, with Sao Tome and Principe named among the seven island states joining a framework that has digital transformation as one of six pillars.
